_comment: Known plug-and-play violations, recorded 2026-07-25 when check-integration-conformance
landed. This is the FIX BACKLOG, not a mute list: every entry is printed on every build,
and an entry that no longer reproduces fails the build so the list can only shrink.
Do NOT add entries to silence a new violation — fix the declaration or the runtime path.
2026-07-25: the five steer:* entries were removed when the model-locked routing clauses
were deleted from the email and calendar tool descriptions. test/tool-description-portability.test.ts
is now the runtime mirror of that check.
2026-07-25: authtype:google removed — google was narrowed to the endpoints an api_key can
actually satisfy, so the finding no longer reproduces. The hardcoded YouTube probe that was
the tell is gone too, replaced by declaration-driven probe headers.
2026-07-26 (C7b): secret:email removed. The finding was a FALSE POSITIVE produced by a stale
checker: it measured the runtime's credentials against the PRIMARY one, asserting 'the install
path persists only the primary', which stopped being true at C5 — resolveInstallValues()
persists every DECLARED credential. CHECK 4 now measures against the declared list, so
'unstorable' means 'resolved or promised but never declared'. Not retired by special-casing
email: the rule changed for every integration, and email simply conforms to it.
2026-07-26 (C7b): transport:email removed. Both halves are now fixed. C7a fixed the agent
prompt (getAgentContext() renders the email_* tools instead of an empty 'Base URL:'); C7b
fixed the route half (/api/integrations/test no longer joins the smtp/imap pseudo-paths onto
an empty baseUrl — it branches on the declared transport and verifies the real SMTP handshake
instead). CHECK 3 now knows the 'transport' field exists: a declared non-HTTP transport is not
a broken HTTP API, and is instead held to its own coherence (unknown transport, or a baseUrl
it contradicts).
